defect.summary: A SINCE BACK-DATED ACROSS A RESTART STILL ENDS A LATCH (S216-2; AA1; audit 2026-10-17 11:22Z): H11 refuses a since moved earlier on a SIGHUP reload only, a restart is a first load, and the stateless reader then receives input byte-identical to an honest grant, so no reader rule can refuse it without false-alarming honesty. T34 prints it as a ceiling until this lands.
defect.ground: Frank's ruling 2026-10-17 15:35Z ('Yes' — a durable grant memory in /var/lib/mica-bridge, effective since = max(declared, first-seen), seeded by Frank at the relay that lands it, its own ticket after T34, a second memory beside the witness accepted as such and printed as one); the audit's 11:22Z ruling (i)-(ii); AA1 receipt option (2); the draft ARC_MICA-TICKET_S216-2-Grant-Memory_DRAFT_v2_20261017.md (v1 refuted under BB2). MECHANISM, MACHINE HALF (per F-1's ruling; shown for F-1 (a), rewritten before signing if (b)): config.harm.grantSince[item][origin] gains declaredAt (ms) and declaredUtc beside at/utc, which now carry the EFFECTIVE since the bridge computed; the reader refuses at < declaredAt whole (HarmMalformed) and refuses a utc or declaredUtc that is not the canonical spelling of its at (pure arithmetic, no Date); config.harm gains grantMemory {tag 'G2_GRANT_MEMORY@'+16 hex, state one of SEEDED, RESEEDED, BEGUN, BEGUN_AFTER_LOSS, RECOVERED_PREFIX, NOT_PERSISTED}, exact keys, so a machine and a bridge of different S216-2-ness read WIRED AND BLIND; granted(r) is unchanged (r.timestamp >= at, window start >= at); every harm verdict that prints a harm basket (SILENT, ALARM, BLIND) prints the memory line beside it, and the reading carries it as grantMemoryLine for /explain; a since that differs from the declared one prints both; the latch-exits text loses 'a restart is a first load: a declaration back-dating a grant across it is not refused today' and the restart half of the grant exit; harm ceilings 17 and 18 are reworded to the effective since and the memory tag; one new harm ceiling line (19). BRIDGE HALF (no door): the memory store, rules GM0-GM5, the effective since, the seeding tool.

arbiter.word: Granted by the audit under Frank's standing delegation, 2026-10-18, on Frank's 'Yes' to S216-2 (2026-10-17 15:35Z) and the rulings of 2026-10-18 06:56Z (8) and 12:08Z: a durable grant memory in the bridge's state directory, hash-chained and append-only, effective since = the latest of the declared since, the bridge's first sight and the high-water since (F-3 yes); unreadable or corrupt → BEGUN_AFTER_LOSS (a loss only ever adds ALARMs); a torn tail → RECOVERED_PREFIX; seeded by Frank at the relay that lands it; never a startup refusal. Conditions of this signature: cond. 5 is signed AS BUILT — the printed line says 'the later of its first sight and the highest since it carried', which is true whichever governs, and naming the governing instant is not demanded (a later tightening may name it); cond. 10 = the measured unseeded prediction (656 and 657 newly ALARM, 654 stays CANNOT_ASSESS); a second memory beside the witness, accepted as such and printed; the machine half (s216-2-on-a0d3017 7ef59150) relays first, then Frank's seed (deploy/seed-grant-memory.sh, 0 traps), then the bridge half (2fa829ef) with its restart; no class or hash moves. expiresAt is the audit's fill and part of this signature.

conditions: 0. PAIRED WITH THE BRIDGE HALF (per F-1's ruling; citadel branch s216-2-grant-memory-bridge off the bridge head relay 2 lands, c9e3a9a if unchanged): the bridge passes the effective since in at/utc, the declared one in declaredAt/declaredUtc, and grantMemory; neither half reads the other's old shape (both refuse whole, BLIND, printing 'Grant memory: not printed'). Relay order: this machine half first, then Frank's seed, then the bridge code with its restart, in one desk session. The bridge relay is code only; the declaration does not change.

1. THE RESTART EXIT IS CLOSED AND ARMED: a latch on record R at T; a restart lays a declaration granting R's origin with a since S <= T; the memory first saw that grant at F > T -> ALARM stands (effective F); the doctor's clearance naming R still ends it. Mutant effective-is-declared -> killed.

2. HONESTY UNCHANGED: with a memory whose first-seens equal the declared sinces, 3000 random fixture books (the T34 removal rehearsal's generator, seed 20261016) read identical to the a0d30173 reader in kind, code, latchedSince and harmLine; a record at the effective since is granted, one ms before is not (killed mutant ge-as-gt kept); an honest LATER declared since than first-seen still governs (killed mutant effective-is-first-seen).

3. LOSS ONLY ADDS ALARMS, ON A CLOCK THAT DID NOT STEP BACK PAST THE CLAMP: over random memory states (missing, begun later, unreadable, torn tail) the set of ALARM readings is a superset of the seeded memory's, never smaller (a monotonicity rehearsal, counts printed); no reading moves to SILENT or to GRANTED by a loss; the clock condition is printed in the ceiling (C2), not assumed away.

4. THE MAX IS A MAX AND THE PRINT IS THE NUMBER (per F-1's ruling): the reader refuses at < declaredAt whole (HarmMalformed, WIRED AND BLIND); a utc or declaredUtc that is not the canonical YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ spelling of its at -> refused (checked by integer arithmetic, no Date); missing declaredAt/declaredUtc/grantMemory, an extra key, a malformed tag or a state outside the six -> refused. Mutants declared-floor-unchecked and spelling-unchecked -> killed.

5. PRINTED AS ONE (per F-1's ruling): every harm verdict that prints a harm basket (SILENT via harmSilent, ALARM, BLIND via harmBlind) prints 'GRANT MEMORY <tag> (<state words>)' beside 'Harm basket:', in fixed words per state; where no validated basket exists (reader threw, harm malformed, including the at < declaredAt refusal and every cross-version reading) it prints 'Grant memory: not printed (no validated harm basket on this path)'; the reading carries the same line as grantMemoryLine (ABSENT on the class path, as harmLine is); the EFFECTIVE since is the latest of three instants: the declared since, the bridge's first sight of the grant, and the highest since the memory carried for it (F-3's high-water, GRANT_SINCE_RAISED); where the effective since differs from the declared one, GRANTED, NONE and the ALARM detail print 'since <utc> (held by the bridge's grant memory: the later of its first sight of the grant and the highest since it carried for it; declared <declaredUtc>)' — true whichever of the two governs, and it does NOT say which; equal sinces print exactly as at a0d30173 and harmLine is unchanged (so T36's live-arc fixture lines stay verbatim). Mutants memory-line-dropped, memory-line-dropped-on-SILENT and declared-not-printed -> killed.

6. THE CEILING TEXT IS TRUE AGAIN: HARM_LATCH_EXITS no longer carries the ruled T34 ceiling sentence or 'a restart takes either' for the grant exit; it says a back-dated grant counts only from the bridge's first sight of it unless that memory is forged or replaced by root, and keeps item removal, origin removal or re-binding, a moved book across a restart, salt-epoch loss and an unreadable predecessor book, each as what it is. Harm ceiling 18 (A GRANT COUNTS FROM ITS SINCE) is reworded to the effective since (the later of the declared instant and the bridge's first sight); harm ceiling 17 (A RESTART IS A FIRST LOAD) names the harmClass AND the memory tag as what shows which stanza and memory read. The T34 arm pinning the old sentence is replaced by arms pinning the new texts; mutants old-sentence-restored and ceiling-18-declared-only -> killed. One new harm ceiling line, count 18 -> 19, naming the second memory, its clock (the bridge's at load, clamped; a step back beyond the clamp and a forward step as C2 says), an unpersisted retirement across a further restart, and root's power over it.

7. NO SERVED LITERAL in the reader or its ceilings; no Date in the reader (the effective and declared UTC spellings arrive injected, are checked arithmetically against their numbers, and are printed as given); the no-timestamp fence's four instant reads unchanged (the new fields are compared, not read as instants of a record).

8. GLUE: the census line (wire.ts gate2HarmCensusLine) prints the memory tag, and gate2HarmReadingReason appends the reading's grantMemoryLine so /explain carries it; those edits and any glue.test.ts change sit under T33's glue document, confirmed by the audit at signature.

9. THE BRIDGE HALF, CONDITIONS FOR ITS ACCEPTANCE (outside the door, stated here so one signature covers the pair): the memory at join(state dir, 'grant-memory'), created with explicit mode 0640 (open mode + fchmod; the dir's default ACL disables the umask) mica-bridge, hash-chained JSON lines, append-only, written under an O_EXCL sibling lock with fsync and ftruncate-back on a failed write; read without the lock; first-seen clamped to the memory's last write and to the newest record in the books the load reads; rules GM0-GM5 as in the draft (the write after the history claim; a SIGHUP before adoption refused; a reload whose retire or raise rows cannot persist refused); never a StartupRefused on the memory's state (the loader's refusal of a declared path that resolves to the memory, its lock or an aside name refuses a declaration, and is said so); a corrupt or unreadable memory moved aside, never edited (per F-2's ruling); a torn last line per F-7's ruling; RESEEDED printed when the event book holds an earlier boundary; the V2 class header reworded (a since moved by the memory moves the tag, not the class); arms for missing, corrupt (flipped byte, extra key, broken chain), torn tail, unwritable (lock held at start: chain adopted, no restamp; EACCES; ENOSPC: no torn tail left), mode of a begun memory = 0640, remove-then-re-add across two restarts (new first-seen), item path changed under one id (new first-seen), origin re-bound (new first-seen), a clock step back (clamped to memory and to books), SIGHUP during start's awaits (refused), and (if F-3 is ruled yes) since raised then lowered across two restarts (high-water holds); mutants retire-skipped, clamp-removed, book-clamp-removed, corrupt-refuses-startup, corrupt-rewritten, tag-without-boundary, state-in-digest, unpersisted-retire-reload-accepted each killed.

10. THE SEED (Frank's hand): ~/mica-relay/s216-2/seed-grant-memory.sh, dry by default, tty refused before anything privileged, run record before sudo, run-stamped tee, no signal trap (S205), required --expect-seed and --expect-declaration (the canonical declarationHash); refuses an existing memory, lock or leftover dot-temp; refuses unless the file's canonical hash, live /status.declarationHash and the candidate's boundary hash all equal --expect-declaration and /status.lastRejectedDeclaration is null; refuses a candidate the release's chain verifier rejects; install -o mica-bridge -g mica-bridge -m 0640 to a dot-temp, the dot-temp hashed as root against --expect-seed before mv -n, mv -n gated on rc and on the dot-temp's absence, the final sha compared against --expect-seed; a dry rig at uid 1000 covers every refusal. The candidate seed is built by the release's own builder from the served declaration; its rows, sha and predicted tag are posted before the act. With the served declaration f8fd37fa (relay 2) it is ONE row: housekeeper / G1 / housekeeper, first seen 2026-10-16T06:13:54.692Z, so decisions 654, 656, 657 read as T36's fixture (measured: seeded live arc 8/8). UNSEEDED (BEGUN at the restart), AS MEASURED by an arm at the build (S216-2 build receipt 2026-10-18, sha 8460c51b…): exactly decisions 656 and 657 newly ALARM; 654 stays CANNOT_ASSESS, its harmLine's grant reading NONE. (v2 predicted all three; the build refuted it, and a ticket never keeps a refuted prediction: audit 2026-10-18 12:08Z.)

11. WHAT THIS TICKET DOES NOT FIX: root can delete (only adds ALARMs; the tag moves), replace (RESEEDED, best-effort) or forge (undetectable: writer, chainer and verifier are one principal) the memory, or run pre-S216-2 code; one kernel clock that steps: a step back beyond the clamp admits a back-dating up to the step (89 backward steps, largest 2.61 s, measured 2026-10-17), a forward step pins new grants into the future; an unpersisted retirement at start can be restored by a further restart (C7, printed); item removal, origin removal or re-binding and a moved book across a restart still end or blind a latch (GM4, printed); the memory is not in the sealed journal; errand-level origin is still S208-2.

12. THE CLASS (per F-4's ruling): recommended, harmClass unchanged (G2_HARM_V2, relay 2's predicted @a1595284d927ca02 stands; this reverses AA1's stated cost and is said so), the memory tag digests boundary and persisted rows but not state, and the sealed-case register keys on (harmClass, memory tag) with a NOT_PERSISTED verdict neither sealing nor voiding; if F-4 rules the fold, the class version becomes G2_HARM_V3 and this condition is rewritten with the predicted class before signing.
